terms.description: Metalworker using an oxy-acetylene torch to cut or weld steel plates in shipyards, boiler shops, and scrap yards.
Tradesman baking bread, rolls, and biscuits in brick ovens.
Guard assigned to railway engineering trains hauling crushed stone (ballast) used to pack and level track beds.
Weaver of willow wicker baskets, hampers, and industrial skeps for docks, markets, and bakeries.
Metalsmith forging wrought iron tools, chains, hinges, and horseshoes at a hearth and anvil.
Worker who crawled inside cooled steam boilers to chip away limescale, soot, and sediment from flues and tubes.
Metalworker who shaped, riveted, and repaired heavy iron and steel plates for steam locomotives, marine boilers, and ships.
Craftsman folding, sewing, and binding printed sheets into leather or cloth-covered books and ledgers.
Tradesman laying bricks and mortar for houses, chimneys, factories, and arches.
Maker of bristle brooms, scrubbing brushes, and industrial brushes.
Building contractor coordinating bricklayers, carpenters, and masons on housing and commercial developments.
Conductor collecting fares and signalling stops on motor omnibuses.
Tradesman slaughtering livestock or dressing and selling meat.
Resident custodian responsible for locking, cleaning, and heating a public building, school, or chapel.
Woodworker framing roofs, floors, and structural timber; 'Joiners' focused on finer interior doors, stairs, and window frames.
Worker managing beer barrels, bottling, and wine cellars for a pub, hotel, or wine merchant.
Originally a maker/seller of candles; in Newport, 'Ship Chandlers' supplied vessels with rope, oil, paint, and provisions.
Woman hired by the day to scrub floors, grates, and steps in offices and private homes.
Pharmacist compounding and selling medicines, tinctures, and household chemicals.
Office worker keeping ledgers, correspondence, shipping manifests, and wages for merchants, solicitors, and docks.
Craftsman constructing wooden bodies for horse-drawn coaches, carts, and railway wagons.
Driver of private horse-drawn carriages or hackney cabs.
Wholesale or retail merchant buying colliery coal by rail wagon and selling it for shipping or domestic grates.
Loaded and evenly distributed coal inside ship holds at Newport Docks so vessels stayed balanced and coal would not shift at sea.
Local representative buying, selling, or shipping goods on commission for collieries, breweries, or manufacturers.
Sales representative travelling by rail between towns with sample cases to take wholesale orders for manufacturers.
Maker and seller of sweets, pastries, cakes, and sugar confectionery.
Craftsman who built and repaired wooden casks, barrels, and tubs bound with iron hoops for beer, butter, and dry goods.
Traditional shoemaker working with fine new leather (distinct from a cobbler, who repaired old shoes).
Wholesale dealer in grain, oats, animal feed, and flour.
Operator of hydraulic or steam cranes hoisting coal wagons and cargo at Newport Docks.
General dockside labourer employed loading and unloading timber, iron, pitprops, and general cargo at Alexandra and Town Docks.
Constable employed by the Alexandra Dock Company or Newport Borough Police to patrol quays, warehouses, and streets.
Retailer of cloth, textiles, haberdashery, and household linens.
Maker of women's and children's dresses, blouses, and tailored daywear.
Driver of a steam locomotive on main lines, colliery branches, or dock sidings (also used for stationary steam engine operators).
Dealer who separated wool from sheepskins and prepared hides for tanners and leather dressers.
Locomotive or boiler crew member who shovelled coal into the firebox and monitored steam pressure and water levels.
Retailer selling fresh and cured fish.
Precision metalworker who assembled, filed, and fitted machined metal parts for engines, railway gear, and dock machinery.
Worker tending blast or reheating furnaces, regulating fuel, air blast, and molten metal tapping.
Employee of the Great Western Railway, which operated Newport High Street station, goods yards, and major South Wales coal routes.
Caretaker of private grounds, or a 'Market Gardener' growing vegetables and fruit for town sale.
Retailer of fresh vegetables, fruit, and potatoes.
Official in charge of a passenger or freight train's safety, braking van, and timetable compliance.
Carrier using horse-drawn wagons or carts to haul coal, stone, timber, and goods between docks, stations, and yards.
Casual dockside worker who assisted with mooring, unmooring, and handling ropes for vessels entering and leaving the Usk and Newport Docks.
Street or shop vendor selling homemade ice cream, often from handcarts.
Agent selling life, fire, and marine policies and collecting weekly premiums door-to-door.
Hardware merchant selling tools, nails, locks, grates, and domestic metalware.
Worker in Newport's iron and steel mills, foundries, or rolling works producing rails, bars, and structural iron.
General manual worker hired for heavy lifting, digging, roadwork, or yard duties across town.
Woman earning a living washing, starching, and ironing linen and clothing by hand.
Operator of a flat-bottomed barge (lighter) ferrying coal, iron, and goods between wharves along the River Usk and larger ships.
Craftsman cutting, dressing, and laying stone blocks for buildings, bridges, and dock walls.
Certified captain qualified to command a merchant vessel; 'Mariner' and 'Seaman' denoted crew serving aboard merchant ships.
Designer, maker, and trimmer of women's hats, bonnets, and headwear.
Early 20th-century term for drivers of petrol lorries, delivery vans, taxis, and private motor cars.
Foundry worker who packed sand moulds around patterns to cast molten iron or brass into machinery parts and pipes.
Shopkeeper selling newspapers, periodicals, books, and writing paper.
Stableman at an inn or coaching house who fed, groomed, and cared for guests' horses.
Retailer selling ready-made clothing, hats, boots, and seafarers' kit.
House, ship, or coach painter applying protective paints, varnishes, and wallpaper.
Licensed mariner with expert knowledge of the Bristol Channel and River Usk tides who guided ships safely into Newport Docks.
Tradesman applying lime or gypsum plaster to interior walls, lath-and-plaster ceilings, and decorative cornices.
Railway trackman responsible for laying, aligning, and maintaining rails and sleepers; a 'Ganger' supervised a track gang.
Tradesman installing lead water pipes, roof flashings, sanitation, and early town gas piping.
Station worker handling passenger luggage, parcels, and platform duties.
Retailer selling poultry, rabbits, and game.
Typesetter and press operator producing newspapers, handbills, and commercial stationery.
Shopkeeper selling staple foods such as bacon, butter, cheese, tea, sugar, and flour.
Highly skilled ironworker who stirred molten pig iron in a reverberatory furnace to burn off carbon and produce wrought iron.
Skilled maritime worker who fitted, repaired, and maintained the standing and running rigging, ropes, and spars of sailing ships.
Mill worker who fed red-hot iron or steel billets through heavy powered rollers to form bars, rails, or plates.
Leatherworker crafting and repairing horse saddles, collars, bridles, and cart harnesses.
Craftsman who cut, stitched, and repaired heavy canvas sails, awnings, and tarpaulins for sailing vessels.
Timber worker cutting logs into planks using either a two-man pit saw or steam-powered sawmill.
Headteacher or master of a National, Board, or private academy.
Skilled carpenter specializing in building, repairing, and caulking wooden hulls and decks of ships.
Railway yard worker who coupled, uncoupled, and directed wagons onto sidings to assemble coal and freight trains.
Operator stationed in a signal box pulling mechanical levers to set points and semaphore signals for safe train movements.
Qualified lawyer advising clients on property, contracts, shipping disputes, and magistrates' court cases.
Worker employed in steelmaking furnaces and rolling mills, increasingly replacing wrought iron from the late 19th century.
Dockworker or contractor responsible for loading and stowing cargo efficiently inside a ship's hold.
Blacksmith's assistant who swung a heavy sledgehammer on hot iron while the smith shaped it with tongs and a hand hammer.
Medical practitioner performing operations and general medical care.
Maker of bespoke men's suits, coats, and waistcoats.
Female garment maker employed in tailoring workshops or from home, often specializing in waistcoats, trousers, or finishing.
Customs officer who boarded incoming merchant ships on the tide to inspect cargo and prevent smuggling before duties were paid.
Craftsman working sheet iron coated with tin to make cans, kettles, lanterns, and domestic utensils.
Shopkeeper selling pipe tobacco, snuff, cigars, and matches.
Conductor collecting fares and managing passengers aboard Newport's street trams.
Driver of horse-drawn or electric street tramcars operated by Newport Corporation.
Operator or engineer aboard steam tugboats towing sailing ships and barges through the River Usk and Bristol Channel.
Craftsman padding, springing, and covering chairs, sofas, and curtains.
Animal doctor essential in an era reliant on pit ponies, haulage horses, and dairy cattle.
Licensed keeper of an inn, tavern, or public house authorized to sell alcoholic drink and food.
Skilled craftsman assembling, cleaning, and repairing pocket watches, clocks, and chronometers.
Keeper or manager of a river or dock wharf, overseeing the landing, storage, and dispatch of cargo and collecting wharfage dues.
Woodworker and smith who built and repaired wooden spoked wheels rimmed with iron tyres for carts and carriages.
Metalworker who pulled heated iron or steel rods through progressively smaller dies to produce wire.
